definition: Visual computing is a generic term for all computer science disciplines dealing with images and 3D models, such as computer graphics, image processing, visualization, computer vision, virtual and augmented reality, video processing, and computational visualistics.
details: Visual computing also includes aspects of pattern recognition, human computer interaction, machine learning and digital libraries. The core challenges are the acquisition, processing, analysis and rendering of visual information (mainly images and video). Application areas include industrial quality control, medical image processing and visualization, surveying, robotics, multimedia systems, virtual heritage, special effects in movies and television, and ludology. Visual computing also includes digital art and digital media studies.

explainer.lead: Visual computing is a generic term for computer science disciplines dealing with images and 3D models, spanning graphics, image processing, visualization, computer vision, virtual and augmented reality, video processing and computational visualistics. It matters because its core challenges—acquisition, processing, analysis and rendering of visual information—underpin many applied fields.

tiers.eli5: It's the umbrella name for all the computer work that involves pictures and 3D models, from making images to understanding them.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners draw on it across application areas such as industrial quality control, medical image processing and visualization, surveying, robotics, multimedia, virtual heritage, film and television effects, and ludology. A pitfall is treating it as one technique when it is a grouping of several disciplines, also including pattern recognition, human computer interaction, machine learning and digital libraries.
tiers.paperLevel: A generic term for computer science disciplines dealing with images and 3D models, with core challenges of acquisition, processing, analysis and rendering of visual information, mainly images and video.

explainer.example: A medical imaging team applies visual computing for image processing and visualization of patient scans.
